plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the single-page MeadowOS marketing site, focusing on navigation, scroll behaviors, interactive modal states, and mobile responsiveness.
plan.summary: The exploration will validate the long-scroll narrative structure of MeadowOS. It will start by testing the top navigation anchor links and scroll progress bar on desktop. Then it will trigger and validate the fake download modal's progression and completion states. Finally, it will evaluate the mobile viewport, paying special attention to the layout of the 'Garden' grid and previously identified small tap targets.
assumptions: The site is a single page (index.html) with internal anchor links.
Clicking the download button triggers a simulated modal rather than an actual file download.
The scroll progress bar updates dynamically as the user scrolls down.
risk_hotspots: Small tap targets in the top navigation and footer links
Fake download modal state transitions (progress to SHA256 verification)
Layout of the 'Garden' 6-card plant-app grid on mobile

phases.title: Navigation and Scrolling
phases.objective: Verify that top navigation links smoothly scroll to their respective sections and the scroll progress bar updates.
key_checks: Click 'Story', 'Garden', 'Docs', and 'Get the .iso' and verify the viewport scrolls to the correct anchors
Observe if a scroll progress bar is visible and updates its width/state based on scroll depth
exit_criteria: All top navigation links have been clicked and their target sections verified.

phases.title: Download Modal Interaction
phases.objective: Test the fake '.iso' download flow and its state changes.
key_checks: Verify a modal appears showing download progress
Wait and verify the progress reaches 100% and displays the SHA256 verification success message
exit_criteria: The download modal has been triggered, fully completed its simulated process, and closed.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport and Layout Validation
phases.objective: Check responsive layout, specifically the 'Garden' grid, narrative text readability, and tap target sizes.
key_checks: Examine the top navigation (check if it collapses or remains thin, verify tap target usability)
Scroll down to the 'Garden' section and ensure the 6-card grid stacks or adjusts appropriately without overflow
Check footer links (GitHub, Matrix room) for accessibility/tap target size
exit_criteria: Mobile layout has been fully scrolled and visually inspected for overflows or usability issues.

coverage_targets.pages: Fully scroll and explore index.html on both desktop and mobile.
coverage_targets.features: Test all anchor links, the fake download modal flow, and hover/active states.
coverage_targets.mobile: Validate mobile layout for the 6-card grid and assess small tap targets identified in prescan.

notes: Pay attention to the typography and 'zine-style' layout elements to ensure they do not break across different screen widths.

prescan_summary.title: MeadowOS — Bring your data home
prescan_summary.visible_text_excerpt: MeadowOS Story Garden Docs Get the .iso Read time · ~6 min Plant your data in a meadow. A small, friendly operating system for your own server. Run the apps you love. Tend them like a garden. A small home for your photos, your notes, your mail, your files. Not in someone else's cloud. I. The Cloud is Someone Else's House. You moved into a place you don't own. You hung your photographs on rented walls. The landlord raised the rent — three times last year. They walked into your bedroom and rearranged the furniture. They told you when guests could visit and which windows you could open. When you complained, they sent you a 47-page Terms of Service in a font designed to discourage you from reading it.
